text:
The right power station depends mostly on what you'll run and how far you'll carry it. For most tent and car camping, a **~250–300Wh LiFePO4 unit** (8–10 lb) covers phones, lights, a fan, and a CPAP for several nights. Step up to **~1kWh+** if you want to run a 12V/electric cooler or kitchen gear.

## Small and light (weekend tent and car camping)

| Model | Capacity / AC output | Weight | Approx. price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288Wh / 300W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | Best overall per PowerStationGearLab: light and simple |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh / 600W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 | Double the inverter and expandable to 572Wh |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh / 300W (600W surge) | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in lantern and 5-year warranty. Buy the AC model, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268Wh / 600W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | Budget pick |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Each pick has a "Check price on Amazon" link on that page. The Jackery 300 Plus has been replaced on Jackery's site by the 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold through Amazon. A tip from the same guide: turn off the CPAP humidifier, or it can triple the power draw.

## Mid-size (cooler, longer trips, car camping)

**BLUETTI AC180**: 1,152Wh LiFePO4 with an 1,800W inverter and 500W solar input. The 5-year warranty applies if you buy from an official store. At about 16 kg (35 lb), it's a car-camping unit, not one to carry far. It has no expansion port.
- $499 at BLUETTI's US store. Code **AFF5OFF** takes 5% off, bringing it to **$474.05**. Dealectric reports the code worked at checkout on 2026-10-21.
- **Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180** (source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
- *Disclosure:* this is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission. The code and test claim come from Dealectric, so confirm the final price at checkout. The $599 option is a bundle with a 100W solar panel.

Other options in this class:
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value at 25 lb and under $530 on sale.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: TechRadar's camping pick.

Sources: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations).

## Big (multi-day off-grid, electric cooler)

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: 2,042Wh in 39 lb, under $900 on Amazon. OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick ([link](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: 1,536Wh, IP65 weather and dust resistant, and drop-resistant. About $1,079 on Amazon. WIRED's camping pick ([link](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)).

**My pick for most campers:** the EcoFlow River 3 Plus, or the Anker C300 if budget matters more. Choose the AC180 or C1000 Gen 2 if you're car camping with a cooler. If you tell me what you plan to power and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow it down.
